A1.justification: The PDFs describe the same work, renamed from FedCADO to FedLMG, with matching guidance losses, aggregation strategies and many results. Both are readable, but v1 includes Appendices A–C whereas v3 ends after the references despite referring to an appendix for proofs, settings and additional experiments. Those unavailable materials limit parts of the comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments, component ablations, heterogeneous-model evaluations and generated-image comparisons, including supplementary results.

after.justification: v3 reports original classification results, loss ablations, communication and computation measurements, and generated-image case studies.

M1.justification: v1 explicitly includes an M-step initial-noise editing stage before diffusion denoising (Section 3.3 and Algorithm 1). v3's stated generation procedure omits this prominent component and describes guided denoising directly. Cross-entropy/BN guidance and the three aggregation strategies remain; renaming and the expanded local-training explanation do not themselves establish further method changes.

E1.justification: Confirmed additions include DomainNet's previously excluded Quickdraw domain and OpenImage privacy cases involving faces, registration plates and notebooks. The three dataset families remain. However, v1's explicit label-skew evaluations have no counterpart in the supplied v3; its missing appendix prevents distinguishing removal from relocation and reliably judging the overall coverage change.

E2.justification: v3 Table 1 adds evaluated FedProx, FedDyn, FedDISC and FGL comparisons; FedDISC and FGL were only discussed in v1. FedAvg, FedDF and centralized training remain. Prompts Only matches v1's SD Gen rather than introducing another comparator. DENSE and FedCVAE remain excluded from the reported quantitative comparisons.

E3.justification: v3 adds evaluation protocols measuring upload/download parameter counts and client FLOPs, plus privacy-oriented generation and visual inspection. Newly evaluated FedDISC uses true labels instead of pseudo-labeling. These expand the evaluation design beyond classification and image-quality comparisons. Changes to retained data splits, sample counts and model configurations cannot be established from the missing appendix.

E4.justification: v3 adds communication/computation analyses (Tables 2–3) and privacy-sensitive image cases (Figure 4). Its displayed ablation compares neither loss, each loss separately and both together, with new visual loss comparisons (Table 4 and Figure 3); v1 instead explicitly tests initial-noise editing alongside the losses. Further claimed supplementary analyses are unavailable.

E5.justification: v1 Appendix B.3 states that results undergo cross-fold validation and are averaged across multiple tests, without specifying run counts. v3 supplies no corresponding statement and its experimental appendix is unavailable. Whether this reporting was retained or revised cannot be determined; neither supplied version presents confidence intervals or error bars.

E6.justification: Matched OpenImage and NICO++ entries in Table 1 remain unchanged, while DomainNet results are replaced under expanded six-domain coverage: the FT average changes from 46.66 to 34.28, which is not a same-setting performance comparison. v3 also adds four baselines' scores, revised ablation results and resource measurements, including 11.69 million communicated parameters for FedLMG.

T1.justification: v1 provides algorithmic equations without a distributional theorem. v3 adds an explicit federated objective, Assumption 1 and Theorem 1 bounding a KL divergence, followed by reasoning connecting local cross-entropy training to that bound. The promised proof is unavailable, and Assumption 1's prose and Equation 4 disagree on the KL direction.

C1.justification: v3 removes initial-noise editing from the headline contributions and adds a claimed theoretical distributional guarantee. It foregrounds avoiding client foundation models and claims no additional client computation or communication burden relative to traditional FL. Heterogeneous-model support and occasionally exceeding centralized training were already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations of client-versus-server computation tradeoffs and attributes multi-teacher performance on DomainNet to overlapping domains. Its privacy discussion shifts from reduced leakage and possible complementary privacy protection in v1 to claiming that extracting specific private information is almost impossible, based on illustrative images. The new Impact Statement also invokes diffusion-model safety checking.

D1.justification: v1's appendices specify pseudocode, architectures, Stable Diffusion v1.5, hardware, learning rates, image counts and splits. v3 refers detailed settings to an absent appendix, so their retention or revision cannot be assessed. Its main text newly discloses one local epoch per communication round for conventional FL comparators, but this does not establish a changed setting for retained experiments.

R1.justification: v3 removes the broad diffusion-model survey and many associated citations, including the initial-noise-editing reference. It adds works concerning FedDyn, FedDEO, CLIP and FL resource constraints, while reorganizing the motivation around the client burden of diffusion-based FL. FedDISC and FGL were already part of v1's research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and contribution list are extensively rewritten. The method narrative is reorganized around local training, generation and aggregation, with a new theoretical subsection and separately expanded aggregation explanations. v3 also introduces Discussions and Limitations and an Impact Statement, alongside the title and method-name changes.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is completely redrawn as a three-stage workflow. v3 Figure 2 combines examples from v1's main text and appendix, adding Quickdraw examples rather than presenting entirely new imagery. Table 1 gains comparator rows and a domain column; new cost tables and loss/privacy figures substantially revise the visual presentation and layout.

improvement.justification: The expanded comparisons, Quickdraw evaluation and resource measurements strengthen the empirical case. However, v3 leaves essential supporting material in an unavailable appendix, introduces a KL-direction inconsistency, and draws strong privacy conclusions from illustrative examples. These benefits, weaknesses and evidence gaps prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
